filters.question: Does it explicitly describe the use of alkaline pretreatment on a substrate
filters.reasoning:
Reasoning: The question asks if the methodology section explicitly describes the use of alkaline pretreatment on a substrate for anaerobic digestion. I will analyze the “2. Materials and methods” section, specifically the subsections related to sample collection and pretreatment procedures, to determine if alkaline pretreatment is explicitly mentioned.

The section 2.1 details the collection of Carica papayas (Pawpaw) peels from Landmark University. Section 2.2 describes the pretreatment procedures. Within this section, it states: “A combination of mechanical and thermo-alkaline pretreatments earlier described (Dahunsi et al., 2016a, b; 2017a) were employed. In doing this, the biomass was grinded into ≤20 mm mesh sizes using a hammer mill and was then followed with a 60 min thermal treatment at 80 °C using the CLIFTON 88579 water bath (Nickel-Electro Ltd., England). This chosen temperature was a modification of previous reports of thermal treatments which documented that higher temperatures adversely affected the overall performance of the anaerobic digestion system (Liu et al., 2012). Heating was then followed by chemical pretreatment using 3 g NaOH for 100 g TS at 55° C for 24 h and a solid loading of 35 g TS/L. NaOH was used since it has been reported as the alkali of choice by previous studies on thermo-alkaline biomass pretreatment (Dai et al., 2016; Dahunsi et al., 2017a, b).”

The key phrase here is “thermo-alkaline pretreatments” followed by the specific use of 3 g NaOH for 100 g TS at 55°C. NaOH is a strong base, and this constitutes alkaline pretreatment.
